title: Grateful Dead Live at Manhattan Center on 1971-04-05
lineage: 7inch 2-track BBD reel (dolby A, 7.5 ips) > PCM501ES@ 44.055 kHz > analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in PCMF1 (Beta HiFi) > PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 @ 48 kHz > DATx4 > Tascam DA-20mkII > M Audio Delta Audiophile 2496 > SoundForge 6.0 (48-44.1)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a high‑energy 4/5/71 show with standout Pigpen‑driven Lovelight, blazing Cold Rain and a monster Truckin > The Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: This board‑tape captures one of the tightest 1971 performances, highlighted by an incendiary second set where Pigpen shines on Lovelight and the band delivers a seamless Truckin > The Other One medley. The audio is crisp and well balanced, making the intricate jams and vocal moments easy to enjoy.

ai_rating.rationale: Across 18 reviews the average rating is 4.56; most reviewers praise both the musical performance (high energy, tight playing) and the soundboard quality (crisp, clear), with only isolated minor criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clean and well‑balanced; no significant dropouts or muddiness reported. Some mention of overdubbed vocals on related releases but the board source itself is praised.

poor_songs: The Other One (some reviewers found it merely okay)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A scorching first set opens with Cold Rain and builds into a tightly knit second set where Pigpen leads on Lovelight and the band rides an intense Truckin > Other One jam; overall flow is cohesive and highly engaging.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is highlighted (yodeling in Bobby McGee, perfect tone), with a note on vocal differences on the NFA track.
band_member_comments.Phil: Frequent 'Philbombs' and thunderous bass that bring the house down during Lovelight and other jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals are noted as different on the NFA version; also praised for rhythm work on Deal.
